epics.title: Frontend Mock Deletion and Live Data Binding
epics.jtbd: When a visitor explores the site, I want to see only real, dynamically updated content from the backend, so that the site reflects my latest thoughts without manual intervention.
epics.sixSigmaMetric: 100% of public content sourced from backend API (0 hardcoded entries)
requirements: R1: All mock data (hardcoded authors, stats, dummy articles) is removed from the frontend codebase.
R2: Empty states in Russian are displayed when no real data exists for a view.
R3: The frontend connects to PodcastEpisodeService, EssayService, and CanonService APIs to fetch content.
R4: Only published podcast episodes (with valid YouTube links) are shown and counted.
R5: The end-to-end integration works seamlessly without manual deployment steps for new content.

epics.title: Sovereign Canon and Ontology Architecture
epics.jtbd: When a visitor explores the site, I want to read the Evergreen manifestos and ontology across structured domains, so that I understand the core architectural philosophy.
epics.tocConstraintRef: Graph traversal and semantic search performance
requirements: R1: Canon concepts are cross-linked with podcast episodes, essays, and sparks.
R2: Instant search (Cmd+K / Ctrl+K) searches the entire corpus conceptually without page reloads.
R3: Every node has a permanent readable URL and clean HTML.
R4: Every node provides machine-readable formats (llms.txt, ai-agent.json, Markdown/JSON).
R5: The author can find concepts and add notes via the interface with minimal friction.

epics.title: Platform Telemetry and Measurement
epics.jtbd: When operating the site, I want to measure visitor engagement with my content and external links, so that I know if the site successfully drives interest in my work. Question 1: Does the concept graph increase multi-page exploration sessions? Question 2: Which newly published content receives the highest visitor engagement? Question 3: Are external AI agents successfully parsing machine-readable endpoints?
requirements: R1: GQM Goal: Understand if the site successfully drives interest. Q1: Does the concept graph increase multi-page exploration sessions? Metric: Track if the unified concept graph and instant search increase cross-content exploration.

R2: GQM Goal: Understand if the site successfully drives interest. Q2: Which newly published content receives the highest visitor engagement? Metric: Measure visitor engagement with newly published content.

R3: GQM Goal: Understand if the site successfully drives interest. Q3: Are external AI agents successfully parsing machine-readable endpoints? Metric: Track the usage of machine-readable endpoints by AI agents.

epics.title: Privacy Consent Management
